body:
#2006 (BUG-1297) — all five acceptance criteria met with named tests, HELD on one branch that can silently reintroduce the defect it fixes.

WHAT IS RIGHT, checked against the acceptance rather than the summary: prefix resolution with an ambiguity error listing candidates; `--in-reply-to` on an unresolvable target now REFUSES rather than warning and detaching; `mailbox thread` accepts a message prefix and distinguishes unknown from empty; and a message is readable without consuming its unread state. That last one cost me real time tonight — one `inbox` call ate a body and the only recovery was reading raw JSON off disk.

THE HOLD:

    Err(error) if error.to_string().contains("ambiguous") => Err(error),
    Err(_) if allow_new => Ok(query.to_string()),

Ambiguity is distinguished from not-found by substring-matching the error's own prose. Reword that message and an ambiguous prefix stops matching the second arm, falls to the third, and on the send path `allow_new` is `true` — so it becomes a NEW THREAD ID.

An ambiguous prefix silently starting a detached thread is exactly the defect this PR was filed to fix. It fails in the permissive direction, and a reword is not something anyone would think to test. The fix is small: type the outcome so the caller matches a variant rather than the text.

It is the BUG-1295 shape in code written after BUG-1295 merged, and I want to be clear that is not a criticism of the lane. It is a reasonable thing to write, which is precisely why the class keeps recurring — which is also an argument for BUG-1310, the external-prose sibling I approved tonight, getting picked up sooner rather than later.

WHY I HELD THIS ONE having lifted three holds an hour ago. The line I drew then: accuracy improvements merge and get filed, failure modes stay held. This is a failure mode — a guard that fails open into the original bug. CI is still pending, so the hold costs nothing yet, and I will take it the moment that branch is typed.

For your picture, the gate now: ten holds. Nine on a change I have specified, one (#1991) because I wrote it and need a reader who is neither of us. Three merged tonight after I lifted their holds, all three auto-completed without manual bumps — TASK-1297, BUG-1279, BUG-1277.
